decision.observation: 4 mph, gear 1, timer 59:59.000, dots pale. High-overhead view: the car sits fully on grass LEFT of the gravel, nose up-frame. The road bends right around a boulder on the right verge, then swings back left into the pines.
decision.hypothesis: The 0.4 s steer cost 15 -> 4 mph and pushed the car off the left edge — steering is far more expensive here than the speed model suggested. The road lies to the car's right, so a long W+D beat should build speed and swing it back onto the gravel, the pattern that worked before from grass.
decision.memory: A 0.4 s W+A at 15 mph costs ~11 mph and drops the car off-road — steering is expensive enough that even short steers need a long throttle beat afterwards. Off-road at 4 mph near boulders: W+D long beat is the recovery.
